the encapsulation of sub-micrometer sized silica particles with a thin shell of polymer, in this case poly(methyl meth-acrylate), can be accomplished in a reaction medium that is free of surfactant or stabilizing agents.
a polymer encapsulation of sub-micrometer sized silica particles is possible by the synthesis of the polymer shells, poly(methyl metacrylate) using the seeding method.

a novel approach to polymer encapsulation of submicrosized inorganic particles by a thin layer of polymer.
the encapsulation of sub-micrometer-sized particles by thin shells of polymer.
the synthesis of silica particles with an encapsulating polymer layer.

this work has shown that a thin coating of polymer can indeed be achieved on silica spheres by a seeding method.

the encapsulation of silica particles by a poly(methylmethacrylate) coating has been demonstrated by the synthesis of the polymer in situ under static conditions in the presence of monodisperse silica spheres.

the synthesis of silica particles is a well established procedure and the synthesis of poly(methylmethacrylate) has been described in literature, but the combination of these two methods has not been described in the past and this is the first time that the synthesis of poly-methylmethacrylateshelled silica particles has been achieved.

we were able to encapsulate silica particles by a polymer shell of poly(methacrylate) using the Stöber process as a synthetic route to monodisperse silica particles.

the encapsulation of silica particles is achieved by a seeding method in a reaction medium containing a precursor for the formation of the silica core, which allows the polymerization of methylmethacrylate to be initiated and propagated in situ on the surface of the silica particles.
the synthesis of silica particles by the Stöber method is an efficient and versatile approach for the encapsulation of silica spheres by a polymeric shell.
